hero.headline: Before asking where the ball should go, ask what boundary must change.
hero.support: A doctrine of space, pressure, possession, promotion, and repair for seeing soccer as the construction and transport of temporary closures through an adversarial field.

sections.heading: Space is actionable, not empty
sections.body: Relevant space depends on reachability, orientation, pressure, support, timing, and what becomes possible after the next action.

sections.heading: Possession is a maintained structure
sections.body: Keeping the ball matters when the team preserves enough support and continuation to transport an advantage rather than merely record completed passes.

sections.heading: Pressure authors futures
sections.body: Effective pressure changes the opponent's reachable action set and can make a later event predictable before it occurs.

sections.heading: Promotion separates motion from progress
sections.body: An advantage is promoted when it survives transport into a more consequential team state.

sections.heading: Repair is tactical intelligence
sections.body: When structure breaks, the next useful question is which repair path restores support, access, responsibility, or control.

built: Analyst vocabulary and tactical tagging concepts
proof.claimBoundary: This is a practitioner doctrine and research on-ramp, not a claim to replace established coaching, performance analysis, or sports science.
